prose: KiviDB is a multi-threaded, Rust-written alternative to Redis and Valkey that speaks the Redis protocol (RESP2 and RESP3), so existing clients, redis-cli and libraries work unchanged - with full-text and vector search built in. It runs every core on a sharded in-memory design and persists via snapshots plus an optional append-only file. The headline benchmark: on the same 32 cores, KiviDB serves 21 million pipelined GETs per second, about 9x Redis 8 and 2.3x Dragonfly, at under half of Dragonfly's p99 latency. It listens on port 6380 by default so it can run side by side with an existing Redis.
highlights: Speaks RESP2/RESP3 - existing Redis clients work unchanged
Full-text and vector search built in
Claims 21M pipelined GETs/sec on 32 cores: ~9x Redis 8, 2.3x Dragonfly
Under half of Dragonfly's p99 latency
Sharded in-memory design with snapshots and optional AOF persistence
Default port 6380 lets it run beside an existing Redis
